title: In an abstract ring, a-a=0, defined generically
statement: For any ring record R (an abstract carrier, additive/multiplicative structure, negation) with sub defined as sub a b := add a (neg b), and element x of R's carrier, sub x x = zero.

formal.statement: theorem Alg.sub_self : ((x0 : Alg.Ring) -> ((x1 : Alg.Ring.carrier x0) -> Eq.{1} (Alg.Ring.carrier x0) (Alg.sub x0 x1 x1) (Alg.Ring.zero x0)))

evidence.supports: Alg.sub (Pi R:Ring, carrier -> carrier -> carrier := fun R a b => R.add a (R.neg b)) and Alg.sub_self (proved by R.negAdd x alone, since Alg.sub R x x unfolds by beta+delta to R.add x (R.neg x)) both admit through the trusted kernel gate. Alg.sub's own specification is confirmed by a symbolic def_eq check against R.add a (R.neg b) at Int.ring (closed over free a b), and Alg.sub_self type-checks symbolically (closed over free x) at both Int.ring and Rat.ring.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- sub_self_and_mul_neg_one_apply_symbolically_at_int_and_rat_rings --nocapture --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out"| grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

evidence.supports: Alg.sub_self instantiated at Rat.ring has the SAME TYPE as the hand-proved Rat.sub_self -- a genuine retirement candidate. Rat.sub itself is already defined as `add a (-b)` (group.rs's declare_subtraction module doc), matching Alg.sub's definition exactly, so this is not a coincidental match.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- retirement_rat_sub_self --nocapture --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out"| grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

notes: Retires Rat.sub_self (same type). Int has no Int.sub_self by that name checked here (out of scope for this fact -- see F:alg-mul-neg-one for the sibling Int-side ring identity coverage).
